title: Burnham urges officials to come up with more radical options for Thames Water
summary: Andy Burnham has told officials to rip up their plans for how to fix Thames Water and present him with more radical options for what to do with the stricken company. In an early test of his promise to bring “the essentials of life” under public control, the prime minister is urging his advisers to g...
content:
Andy Burnham has told officials to rip up their plans for how to fix Thames Water and present him with more radical options for what to do with the stricken company.
In an early test of his promise to bring “the essentials of life” under public control, the prime minister is urging his advisers to go back to the drawing board and create a new list of policies for the utility.
One option being looked at is to convert about £100m of outstanding fines into a government stake in the company, saving its creditors money but giving ministers some say in how it is run.
Burnham previously said he would nationalise Thames, which is running out of cash and recently asked its creditors for an additional £2.4bn, but is struggling to find a way to do so without spending billions of pounds, getting tied up in a lengthy court battle, or both.
Sources familiar with the prime minister’s thinking say he has now told policy officials across Whitehall to contemplate options that were not previously considered feasible, even if that means spending taxpayer money and going to court.
One government source described the fate of the company as a “litmus test” on whether the government could deal with challenges in the medium term, rather than just immediate cost of living support and longer-term structural changes.
“There are more options than people have assumed to date including ones that have never been properly considered,” the source said.
Another said the prime minister had told his officials to “look at all the options and not feel constrained”, in a departure from the advice under Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer.
Burnham has promised to end what he calls “40 years of neoliberalism” and has instructed his ministers to draw up a 10-year plan for government later this year, including detailed proposals for bringing utilities under public control.
Meanwhile, Angela Eagle, the environment secretary, is working on a water bill that will lift a Thatcher-era cap on government ownership of water companies and could rewrite how the bankruptcy regime works for the industry.
Government advisers believe changes to the “special administration regime” (SAR) would make it easier to take companies such as Thames into state control in the future.
But Burnham is also looking for a more immediate solution to Thames’s problems.
When the prime minister came to office, government insiders say he was presented with two main options for Thames: strike a bailout deal with the American hedge funds that own its debt, or pursue an SAR.
Thames’s creditors had proposed a £10bn rescue plan for the company, but Emma Reynolds, the previous environment secretary, made clear her opposition to such a plan before Burnham became prime minister.
Government lawyers also believe it will be difficult to have the company placed into SAR given that it is being kept afloat financially by its creditors and has managed to keep services running.
Among the other options being discussed is the waiving of the approximately £100m in environmental fines the company still owes and taking a stake in it instead. Then, if and when the company is fined again, the government would automatically increase its share rather than collecting the cash.
While some believe this would be a relatively straightforward way to give the government a say in how the company is run, many also believe it would fall short of Burnham’s promise to nationalise the company outright.
The prime minister is under pressure to go further, for example by stripping Thames of its licence, pushing for it to go into SAR immediately and then taking it out of administration without offering anything to the existing creditors.
Such a plan will inevitably be challenged in court, but Burnham is understood to be more willing to take on legal action than Starmer was. One adviser said: “Litigation was always a 100% certainty.”
The prime minister’s advisers also believe they can go further with Thames than with other companies because international investors see the company as a unique case, and not an indication of how the government intends to treat every water company.
Officials say other water companies are likely to be dealt with in different ways, through a mixture of stricter regulation and increased oversight by elected officials such as mayors.
Ewan McGaughey, a professor in law at King’s College, London, said: “The government’s best option is to start a special administration process for Thames Water before it runs up more debts, and sends billions more overseas.
“An orderly transition to public ownership does not require that banks in control are bailed out – on the contrary, the law says polluters should pay.”
Lena Swedlow, deputy director of the Compass campaign group, said: “The obvious solution is to put Thames Water into SAR, and then brought into public ownership so it truly works for everyone.
“While reform of the failing regulatory mechanisms is welcome, any recapitalisation and debt-to-equity schemes that do not seek to permanently wrestle the company from private hands will fail to be in the interests of the workers, stakeholders, and the 16 million people Thames serves. Everything else is noise in the wind.”

title: Meloni envía 500 soldados a Milán tras dos noches de incidentes y saqueos
summary: Meloni envía 500 soldados a Milán tras dos noches de incidentes y saqueos La ciudad ha amanecido traumatizada, con un fuerte despliegue policial en el Duomo y decenas de padres esperando en comisaría a 271 chicos detenidos El Gobierno italiano de Giorgia Meloni ha decidido enviar a Milán 500 soldado...
content:
Meloni envía 500 soldados a Milán tras dos noches de incidentes y saqueos
La ciudad ha amanecido traumatizada, con un fuerte despliegue policial en el Duomo y decenas de padres esperando en comisaría a 271 chicos detenidos
El Gobierno italiano de Giorgia Meloni ha decidido enviar a Milán 500 soldados para garantizar la seguridad de la ciudad tras dos noches consecutivas de caos y saqueos en el centro, en una emulación de lo sucedido en Francia. Lo ha anunciado el vicepresidente y líder de La Liga, Matteo Salvini, milanés, este lunes por la tarde como parte de un decreto con nuevas medidas de seguridad que el Consejo de Ministros aprobará probablemente el martes. Meloni ha mantenido una reunión con varios ministros y responsables de seguridad para acordar algunas decisiones, como extender el arresto preventivo a menores de edad, según los medios italianos. Es una medida aprobada recientemente que permite retener antes de una protesta a los sospechosos de posibles actos violentos. También se baraja la prohibición de reunirse en grupo en lugares públicos a los menores detenidos.
El día después de los disturbios en el centro de Milán, por segunda noche consecutiva, la plaza del Duomo está llena el lunes de furgones de la policía. A primera hora de la tarde, agentes antidisturbios aguardan con sus escudos en las esquinas. Cuando empieza a caer el sol crece el temor y la tensión, entre el jaleo de turistas, porque no se sabe si habrá también una tercera noche de incidentes. Milán es una ciudad traumatizada, tras ver violentas escenas de grupos armados con barras de hierro que rompían escaparates y saqueaban tiendas de ropa para llevarse zapatillas de marca, o móviles en locales de telefonía, o asaltaban supermercados para robar tartas y hasta se llevaban bicicletas del Decathlon de Piazza Cairoli.
De momento, hacia las siete de la tarde se ha registrado una trifulca en Corso Vittorio Emanuele, donde un grupo de simpatizantes de la derecha había colocado una pancarta con la frase “Os remigraremos a todos”, pues parte de los participantes en los disturbios eran italianos de segunda generación, nacidos en Italia de padres inmigrantes. El apelativo desdeñoso con el que se les llama, en concreto a los que se visten con ropa deportiva y un cierto estilo callejero, es “maranza”. Un grupo de jóvenes se ha acercado a increparles por la pancarta y ha empezado una pelea con insultos y el lanzamiento de petardos. Ha tenido que intervenir la policía.
Han contribuido a caldear más el ambiente unas declaraciones del famoso rapero milanés Marracash, que no es un chaval, tiene 47 años, pero es un referente de miles de jóvenes por sus letras de denuncia y en redes sociales ha escrito: “Me esperaba esta reacción desde hace tiempo y creo que estamos solo al principio. Por las buenas no cambias las cosas”.
La mayoría de las tiendas de marcas de lujo de calle Monte Napoleone, la más exclusiva de Italia, han cerrado a las dos de la tarde. Versace, Gucci, Prada, casi todas. En el llamado cuadrilátero de la moda muchos locales de todo tipo han echado también la persiana.
En calle Torino, la gran vía comercial que sale de la plaza del Duomo se ven escaparates rotos la noche del domingo. “Empezaron a romper todo, tuvimos que meter a los clientes dentro y cerrar las puertas”, cuenta un camarero del bar Granaio, que está colocando las mamparas de cristal de la terraza, medio rotas. Pero muchos otros bares quitan las mesas cuando avanza la tarde.
Entre una tienda de Foot Locker y otra de Champion, que fueron saqueadas y están cerradas, agentes de paisano registran a siete chicos. Todos vestidos de negro con ropa deportiva, el uniforme de estas movilizaciones. Todos con aspecto de ser menores de edad o casi. Varios de ellos, italianos de segunda generación. Los alrededores del Duomo están llenos de policías de calle, este lunes el objetivo es que los chavales no lleguen a juntarse en la plaza, pararlos antes.
Pero el problema, según explican las autoridades en los medios, es que no se sabe bien de dónde salen estos jóvenes ni qué quieren, no tienen mensajes políticos, no están organizados, acuden llamados por mensajes en Tik Tok y Telegram, y luego se mueven espontáneamente en grupos dispersos recorriendo la ciudad. Es pura rabia de descontento social. La etiqueta que les ha movilizado es simplemente “#italiainpiazza” (Italia en la calle). De hecho, se han visto en los disturbios banderas italianas, pero también palestinas y de otros países, como Albania, Marruecos y Túnez.
Muchos de estos jóvenes son de las afueras de Milán, una ciudad cada vez más rota por las desigualdades económicas, y llegan el fin de semana en tren de los municipios del norte hasta la estación Milano Centrale. En otras ciudades del norte, como Bérgamo, Brescia, Turín y Verona, se registraron también altercados la noche del sábado, además de en Bolonia, la única ciudad más al sur donde ha habido incidentes.
“Acciones destructivas de rara violencia”
La noche del domingo se juntaron en Milán en torno al Duomo unos 2.000 jóvenes, según las fuerzas del orden. De ellos, 271 acabaron detenidos y 220 eran menores, el 80%. La mayoría son italianos y 60, extranjeros. Para comprender quiénes son un buen lugar ha sido la puerta de la comisaría de calle Fatebenefratelli, donde desde primera hora de la mañana decenas de padres y madres esperaban que los soltaran. Italianos, egipcios, tunecinos, ucranios. Preocupados, muchos de ellos muy enfadados, con ganas de echarle la bronca a su hijo. Algunos descubrieron que su hijo estaba detenido con la localización del móvil. Otros lo vieron incluso en vídeos colgados en redes sociales, que mostraban cómo lo arrestaban.
Los autos de los fiscales donde piden al juez la custodia cautelar de al menos 11 de los detenidos usan palabras duras: han mostrado “una significativa capacidad criminal” con “acciones improvisadas destructivas y de rara violencia”. Las acusaciones son de devastación y saqueo, que implican penas de hasta 15

title: France imposes partial curfews in several cities, including parts of Paris
summary: Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris, after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests around the country. Sébastien Lecornu, the French prime minister, said after an emergency cabinet meeting on Monday he was...
content:
Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris, after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests around the country.
Sébastien Lecornu, the French prime minister, said after an emergency cabinet meeting on Monday he was “fully resolved to restore public order” and had called for “local and partial” curfews if needed. There was “no question” of imposing a full curfew on entire cities, he said.
His office later announced partial curfews from 8pm to 6am on Monday and Tuesday nights in four northern cities, including Lille.
Police also imposed a curfew from 11pm on Monday until 6am on Tuesday in two areas in Paris: Place de la République, where rioting took place on Saturday; and the shopping neighbourhood of Les Halles, which has been subject to looting.
A statement from police said the orders banned gatherings and demonstrations and prohibited anyone from entering or remaining in the two designated areas.
France’s second city, Marseille, earlier announced independently that it had banned all gatherings and demonstrations on Monday. French unions, meanwhile, called for a new round of strikes and rallies on 5 November.
Lecornu told reporters that if declaring a state of emergency was deemed necessary “we could do so”, but added that at this stage partial curfews seemed “more appropriate”.
Lecornu’s comments came after France’s interior minister conceded that police had “lost control” in some cities during Saturday’s protests and the president, Emmanuel Macron, demanded a full security review and “new operational methods” to end the rioting.
Laurent Nuñez said on Monday there had been a “lack of anticipation” in preparations for the protests and acknowledged that police numbers had sometimes been inadequate to deal with rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations.
Nuñez said intelligence had suggested there would be 200,000 demonstrators around the country. In the event, there were more than 500,000 and peaceful protests were hijacked, morphing into one of France’s most violent days of unrest in recent years.
He said he had tendered his resignation to Macron because he felt “responsible for everything that happened”. Macron refused it, demanding instead that Nuñez “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over planning and intelligence failures”.
The protests follow weeks of demonstrations by high school students that have been marred by sometimes violent clashes with police, rocking the country six months before a crunch presidential election and amid mounting economic pressures.
Public buildings including a town hall were attacked and set ablaze and an estimated 2,000 shops were ransacked and looted, authorities have said.
France’s digital minister, Anne Le Henanff, urged online resale platforms to remove listings for “stolen items” and summoned representatives of companies including Vinted and eBay. According to the commerce ministry, representatives of Amazon, Leboncoin, Meta and TikTok were also invited.
Nuñez said 60,000 police and other security forces had been deployed around the country, but acknowledged it had not been enough to control determined, organised groups of violent rioters in major cities including Paris, Marseille and Lyon.
“You couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and say we hadn’t lost control,” the minister told French radio, but added that the responsibility of “rioters, looters and ultra-left militants” should not be glossed over.
The justice minister, Gérald Darmanin, also said intelligence failings had left the state vulnerable. “There’s no good policing without good intelligence,” he said, adding that many of those arrested had police records and “about 80%” were being prosecuted.
Darmanin said 2,513 people had been arrested and 67 imprisoned since the violence broke out over the weekend, Libération reported.
Some 70% of those arrested were adults and almost 1,000 police and gendarmes have been injured.
 
Macron’s office said in a statement on Monday that besides reviewing the security shortcomings, Nuñez had been tasked with “promptly implementing new operational methods for security forces to use on the ground in combating rioters”.
Rioting and looting continued on Sunday. The mayor of Paris, Emmanuel Grégoire, said on Monday that about 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, with a further 350 people arrested overnight.
“Maintaining public order is the responsibility of the state. It is the state that was at fault this weekend,” Grégoire said. “We have a social movement that is spreading, and no political prospect for a constructive way out. So the protests will continue.”
Marseille’s mayor, Benoît Payan, said not just democracy but “the very foundations of the Republic” had been undermined. Describing the situation as “almost insurrectional”, he said the government’s stance amounted to “petty political manoeuvring”.
On Monday, protesters blocked entrances to the Louvre Museum in support of the nationwide high school student protest movement and to denounce “police repression”. The museum could not open as scheduled because of the protest.
A leaflet displayed outside the museum read: “We are proud to announce that we are blocking the world’s largest museum.”
In a televised address on Sunday, Macron criticised the “unbridled” violence and said local authorities would be able to ban some demonstrations in the coming days, but stopped short of drastic measures such as declaring a state of emergency or curfew.
Saturday’s protests, by students, teachers, parents, unions and workers, focused on the high cost of living, an issue that also prompted demonstrations in several other European countries including Italy, Belgium and Albania over the weekend.

title: Israeli police detain 10 people in rare raid against West Bank settlers
summary: Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist Heidi Levine, which she described as an “attempted lynching”. She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked I...
content:
Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist Heidi Levine, which she described as an “attempted lynching”.
She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked Israeli men as she covered the olive harvest in a Palestinian village on Friday. The militants broke four vertebrae and a rip, ripped open her finger so it required surgery and left her with lacerations across her body.
“I was practically, basically lynched by a gang of Jewish settlers in the area of Ramallah,” Levine said, in an interview with the BBC from her hospital bed on Monday.
The day after that assault, Israeli militants armed with sticks and iron bars attacked a group of European diplomats and Palestinians harvesting olives outside the town of Taybeh, assaulting a visiting French mayor, smashing the window of an official car, and causing severe injuries to a young Palestinian man.
The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, questioned the accounts of Israeli militant violence, ignoring extensive video and witness evidence.
He referenced an “alleged attack” on Levine, whose severe injuries were visible in interviews from her hospital bed, and “unproven allegations” the diplomats had been targeted by militants.
The attacks and his response drew a furious international reaction, including from the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee – generally considered a staunch ally of the current Israeli government – European nations and the editor of the Washington Post, Matt Murray.
On Monday morning Israeli police released footage of a rare raid on settlers, and said they had detained 10 people connected with the attacks on foreigners and construction of an illegal outpost.
Hours later a court extended the detention of six men connected with the attacks on foreigners, to between three and four days.
There has been little response to extreme violence against Palestinians across the West Bank, and Levine said the global focus on her attack highlighted extreme double standards.
“People are dealing with this, undergoing attacks, losing property, losing family members, being injured all across the West Bank and nothing is being done,” she said.
Israelis target Palestinians with near total impunity in the occupied West Bank, where arrests are unusual, indictments rare and convictions even more unusual.
Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has documented 561 incidents of settler and soldier violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank over three weeks since 27 September. That is an average of more than 26 each day.
“It is telling that it took attacks on foreign nationals to prompt a significant response from Israeli authorities,” said the group’s executive director, Ziv Stahl. “Palestinians have endured years of systematic settler violence, with 94% of investigations into cases of settler violence against Palestinians closed without indictments.
Levine said her body armour and helmet had prevented even more serious injuries, and she considered herself “lucky” given the ferocity of the attack. Netanyahu’s attempt to cast doubt on the attack felt like a “a big slap on my face”, she added.
Netanyahu’s statements, apparently undermined by security forces arrests days later, were widely seen as an attempt to court far-right voters inside Israel, as the country heads into the final days of an election campaign.
His coalition partners include extremist settlers, who support the campaign of violence that has driven thousands of Palestinians from their homes and land in the occupied West Bank over the last three years.
Haaretz reported on Monday that political pressure was preventing the army from confronting “Jewish terrorism” in the West Bank, even when the targets were foreigners including diplomats and journalists.
Commanders are reluctant to challenge settler leaders, or take action against Israeli civilians and soldiers who attack Palestinians, Israeli defence officials told the paper.
Formal investigations and disciplinary procedures are limited and undermined by unofficial but clear messages of support from top commanders, the report said.
It cited the response to an attack on a CNN crew in March. Central Command chief Maj Gen Avi Bluth suspended the battalion responsible from operational duty and announced disciplinary action against soldiers involved.
Later that night, the brigade commander came to a base where the soldiers were staying to express his support and join them in prayer, Haaretz said.

title: ITV’s exposé of racism and misogyny in Reform? Just a few (more) bad apples | John Crace
summary: It was the dog that didn’t bark in the night. After Sunday night’s ITV exposé of widespread racism and misogyny within Reform, you might have expected one of its MPs to have taken to the airwaves on Monday morning to defend the party’s honour. To try to persuade viewers that the real problem lay wit...
content:
It was the dog that didn’t bark in the night. After Sunday night’s ITV exposé of widespread racism and misogyny within Reform, you might have expected one of its MPs to have taken to the airwaves on Monday morning to defend the party’s honour. To try to persuade viewers that the real problem lay with the journalists who couldn’t stop themselves from investigating Reform rather than the fact that the party’s bigotry was endemic.
Instead, we got nothing. Every Reform MP was otherwise engaged. Were too busy having breakfast. Nothing from Nigel Farage. Nothing even from Robert Jenrick. Maybe he realised he had crashed and burned a few days earlier by suggesting it was just one of those things. One of life’s little mysteries. The BBC was riddled with paedophiles and Reform was awash with racists, said Honest Bob. No big deal. Every organisation had its crosses to bear.
The only MP to post on X in the morning was Richard Tice, who was feeling decidedly grumpy, having only just got married to Isabel Oakeshott. Perhaps he had a hangover. Though his main gripe was that British Airways was yet another failing British institution because it had mislaid at least one of his bags.
Dicky’s social media post had more than a touch of the “don’t you know who I am” to it. You can only imagine the baggage handler may have known exactly who Dicky was and had taken great pleasure in diverting one of the fake Louis Vuitton suitcases from Dubai to Manila. Via Buenos Aires.
The one person out and about for Reform was the one person you would have thought the party would want to keep hidden. Step forward Matt Goodwin, the party’s failed candidate for the Gorton and Denton byelection whose own views could easily pass off as borderline racist in polite circles. Matt is going through his own personal anti-growth agenda. Working hard to deconstruct himself from low-level academic to incredibly dim primate with low social skills. Almost every day, voters in Gorton and Denton thank their lucky stars for having dodged that bullet.
Matt’s defence of Reform was … unorthodox, to put it kindly. So much so that you began to wonder whether he was even conscious. Luckily for him, he was only allowed out on Times Radio. Though that was more than enough. To try to understand Matt is to make a category error. The whole point is to not understand him. That’s the way you stay sane. Because what he wanted listeners to believe was that Nige was a buffer zone against racism. That hordes of would-be racists begged to be allowed to join Reform, only to find out that Nige was a man of peace and love. The one politician who wanted nothing but good things for all immigrants.
It got better. Because Batshit Matt also wanted us to believe that the ITV documentary had just uncovered a few bad apples in the party. So in a way it had done Reform a favour. What were the chances? The ITV journalists had managed to uncover the only seven racists in the Reform ranks. Everyone else was Team Nigel. Never had a bad word for anyone. Except, there was another way of looking at this. That ITV had filmed about 10 Reform councillors and found that seven of them had views that included beheading King Charles for being a Muslim. Some statisticians might put that down as a 70% hit rate. Not so much a few wrong ’uns but a whole army of them. Poor Nige. Always the victim.
Over in the Commons, Wes Streeting was preparing for other threats during departmental defence questions. Though John Healey was not one of them. You’d have thought that Wes might have wanted to schmooze the chancellor before next week’s budget. To try to get the best funding settlement he could. Not a bit of it. Wes began by slagging off his predecessor as defence secretary for wasting money on unnecessary training exercises and then announced he was confident that Healey would reach the necessary 3% and 3.5% targets at next year’s spending review. So, no, Wes wouldn’t be resigning any time soon. Let’s hope his confidence is well placed.
Instead, Wes seemed more interested in persuading himself that there was absolutely nothing unusual in Donald Trump switching the Starlink satellite system on and off at random moments, thereby allowing Russian drones to do untold damage on Ukraine. This was just standard procedure. The only way you could tell the system was working properly was if you turned it off from time to time. Obvious when you think about. Wes was also totally chilled about Trump trying to lower US pump prices by allowing Russian imports of diesel. Fuel that the Russians had also imported from Iran and with whom, coincidentally, the US was at war.
All of this apparently made perfect sense not just to Streeting, but also to Labour and opposition backbenchers. Wes could reassure us because he had had a personal meeting with Pete Hegseth the previous week, during with the secretary for war had reiterated Trump’s claims that Nato forces had been a waste of space in Afghanistan and that the US troops had fought alone. A nice ice breaker. After that, Pete went out of his way to say Washington was totally behind Ukraine, just so long as Russia won the war.
Curiously, the shadow defence secretary, James Cartlidge, didn’t use his questions to talk up the four drones of the “Britannia shield” that the Tories were sure would protect the UK from nuclear war. So it remains a mystery. Almost as if it was a bullshit party conference announcement that was designed to be forgotten within days. Highlight of the day went to Sharron Davies, the former swimmer turned Tory peer, who demanded to know why Andy Burnham hadn’t invaded France to stop the rioting. Can you explain it to her?

title: Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie finally set for Glasgow debut
summary: Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie set for Glasgow debut - Published Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut. The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been side...
content:
Ex-Scotland captain Ritchie set for Glasgow debut
- Published
Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut.
The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been sidelined for the opening months of the season because of ankle and Achilles tendon issues.
The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, is now back in full training and is expected to play in Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) match against Benetton in Treviso.
"He's training fully. We feel he's integrated into the systems now very well. And he's itching to go," said Carolan.
"It would be great if we get him involved this week, either starting or on the bench. It would be really positive to have him involved, especially ahead of Scotland's Nations Cup in a couple of weeks."
Ritchie was a pillar of the Edinburgh team for more than a decade before moving to the French Top 14 side.
Carolan believes patience will pay off for the Warriors with Ritchie, who has moved to Scotstoun on a two-year deal.
"I think it was important to get the timing right. We didn't want to rush him," the Irishman added.
"Obviously he had surgery over the summer so we didn't really want to push him. He's just moved to a new club and with all that going on, we felt the timing needed to be right.
"We could have involved him maybe last week but that was Ruwald van der Merwe's time. So I think the time has now come to unleash Jamie Ritchie in a Glasgow Warriors shirt."
Warriors are second in the URC table after three matches - behind Edinburgh - and will be favourite against second-bottom Benetton this weekend.
They finished top of the URC last season but were knocked out of the play-offs in the semi-finals by the Bulls and the arrivals of Ritchie and Van der Merwe - with Scotland back row Jack Dempsey departing - were part of an evolution of Franco Smith's squad in the summer.

title: Christiane Amanpour anuncia que deja la CNN después de 43 años como referencia del periodismo internacional
summary: Christiane Amanpour anuncia que deja la CNN después de 43 años como referencia del periodismo internacional La decisión se produce unas semanas después de que Paramount Skydance, de la familia Ellison, cerrara la compra de Warner Bros., propietaria de la popular cadena de noticias La prestigiosa per...
content:
Christiane Amanpour anuncia que deja la CNN después de 43 años como referencia del periodismo internacional
La decisión se produce unas semanas después de que Paramount Skydance, de la familia Ellison, cerrara la compra de Warner Bros., propietaria de la popular cadena de noticias
La prestigiosa periodista de CNN Christiane Amanpour ha anunciado este lunes que abandonará la cadena de noticias a partir del próximo junio. “Tras muchos meses de reflexión y algunas noches sin dormir, he decidido separarme de CNN, mi socio durante 43 fantásticos años”, declaró la presentadora de 68 años a través de un comunicado.
Amanpour es una referencia en el periodismo televisivo. Es una de las reporteras especializadas en información internacional con más reputación en la profesión. Ha cubierto varias guerras y crisis internacionales, como la caída del Muro de Berlín, la guerra de Bosnia, la guerra del Golfo Pérsico, la guerra de Irak posterior al 11-S, Afganistán, la Primavera Árabe, la invasión rusa de Ucrania y la guerra de Israel en Gaza.
Además, ha entrevistado a una multitud de líderes internacionales a los que ha formulado preguntas incisivas. Aún se recuerdan sus cara a cara con presidentes como Bill Clinton; el ex primer ministro británico Tony Blair, el exlíder libio Muamar Gadafi y el exlíder iraní, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
La salida de la reportera se produce justo después de que CNN haya caído en manos de David Ellison. Paramount Skydance, la empresa que preside, se ha hecho con Warner Bros. por algo más de 110.000 millones de dólares, deuda incluida. Ellison consiguió crear un imperio del entretenimiento y mediático gracias al apoyo de su padre, Larry Ellison, uno de los hombres más ricos del mundo debido a las acciones que posee de la empresa tecnológica Oracle. Ellison es también uno de los grandes apoyos del presidente Donald Trump. Es uno de sus mayores donantes y amigo personal. El mandatario republicano lleva meses con una campaña de desprestigio contra la CNN y sus periodistas porque no le gustan sus informaciones. La cadena, por el contrario, goza de gran credibilidad y es uno de los referentes del periodismo televisivo en Estados Unidos.
Amanpour aseguró en el comunicado que siempre apoyará a CNN y su tradición de periodismo independiente. El director ejecutivo de CNN, Mark Thompson, comunicó la noticia al personal: “Christiane ha reflexionado detenidamente sobre esta decisión, y llevamos varios meses hablando de ello”, escribió. “Al igual que muchos empleados de CNN que se enterarán hoy, lamento mucho su partida, pero he llegado a aceptar que este es el momento adecuado para ella, tanto en lo personal como en lo profesional”.
Amanpour había expresado públicamente su preocupación porque CNN cayera en manos de la familia Ellison. Hace un par de meses, cuando aún faltaban algunos flecos por cerrar para que la fusión entre Paramount y Warner fuera efectiva, aseguró: “Claramente estoy preocupada, y no estoy segura de cuánto me está permitido decir sobre un asunto corporativo en marcha, pero obviamente estoy preocupada, como persona, como periodista con una trayectoria, y estoy preocupada en base a lo que ha sucedido con las otras cosas que [Ellison] ya ha adquirido, como CBS News”.

title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
summary: At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to ha...
content:
At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.
The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.
There will be an inquiry into how so many troops were left so exposed to a Houthi attack. In mid-September, the group began a fresh push on forces backing the UN-recognised government by pushing south along the Red Sea coast to try to take control of the Bab al-Mandab waterway.
Reliable assessments of the death toll in the fighting over the last month are hard to gather, but it is running into the many thousands. A Saudi airstrike on Sunday killed nine, including five children and two women.
Rashad al-Alimi, the president of the UN-recognised government, said those killed on Monday were new recruits, and he vowed an immediate hard response. He said the incident “affirmed that targeting the recruits reflects the Houthi militias’ approach of resorting to cowardly terrorist attacks whenever they face pressures or their Iranian-backed sabotage plots falter”.
On Monday he phoned the UN secretary general, António Guterres, to ask for the UN to classify the Houthis as a foreign terrorist organisation.
The Shabwa provincial authority said: “Targeting recruits constitutes a military escalation and a blatant assault on the province’s security.” Its governor, Awad bin al-Wazir, visited the wounded in hospitals, and called for extra air defences, saying troops were fighting across six fronts.
The killings underline the dangers of large numbers of troops gathering in one place within reach of the Houthi ballistic missile arsenal. The training camp was struck by three ballistic missiles while the recruits lined up in formation.
Houthi forces have also cut the road between government-run Shabwa and the Houthi-run Bayda governorate.
The Houthi military spokesperson said: “Our armed forces targeted the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations in al-Alam camp, which is run by Saudi officers in the eastern regions. The targeting resulted in the fall of dozens of dead and wounded from the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations, including Saudi officers.
“We warn the deceived ones against responding to the Saudi enemy’s calls to lure them with his defiled money to the pyres of death, and to exploit them instead of his soldiers who are indifferent to their lives.”
A Yemen government spokesperson said the site struck was not a military target linked to the current fighting but “a training centre where new recruits in the internal security forces of Shabwa governorate receive training and qualification programmes.”
They added: “This reveals the criminal nature of this assault, which targeted young people in the preparation and qualification phase to carry out their security duties, far from the frontlines.”
Separately the Houthis claim to have hit the anti-Houthi Giant Brigades of southern Yemen in six strikes in the areas of al-Suqya and Ras al-Ara. Southern forces are said to have been making progress in edging Houthi forces out of control of the area around the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrowest waterway taking ships from the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.
Fighting is also under way as Houthis try to mount a siege of Taiz, where citizens have been calling for greater air protection. In the city there seems to be a determination not to capitulate, but conditions are deteriorating as Houthis close access points.
It is not clear whether the Houthis have decided to slow the pace of attacks on Saudi airports and energy installations, or they are running low on munitions.
The Saudi Aramco headquarters was struck last weekend and some airlines have said they will not yet resume using Riyadh airport. The airport reopened at the weekend after being attacked this month.
Egypt’s parliament has postponed a vote on whether to send troops to Saudi Arabia despite extending the debate to a second day as MPs demanded more than two minutes each to speak. The vote is now likely to be held next week.
A two-thirds majority is required, and some opposition parties have signalled their intention to vote against or abstain. Disputes centre on the extent of the mission and whether it will involve sending troops into Yemen to help Saudi Arabia, and whether Egyptian troops inside Saudi Arabia would become targets for Houthi attacks.
The delay also gives the Egyptians time to see if Iran can persuade the Houthis to hold back, and for Saudi Arabia to confirm the renewal of badly needed loans to Egypt.
Egypt has resisted any ground intervention in Yemen, dating back to the 1962-67 war, when Gamal Abdel Nasser sent troops to back the republicans in North Yemen against the Saudi- and British-backed royalists. The incursion was intended to be minimal, but escalated to as many as 70,000 soldiers. Estimates of Egyptians killed range from 10,000-26,000.

summary: Netflix emitirá ‘La velada del año’ de Ibai Llanos en directo los próximos tres años El evento creado por el creador de contenido amplía así su alcance a una audiencia global y llega a la plataforma que también compró los derechos del Mundial 2030 La velada del año se retransmitirá en Netflix durant...
content:
Netflix emitirá ‘La velada del año’ de Ibai Llanos en directo los próximos tres años
El evento creado por el creador de contenido amplía así su alcance a una audiencia global y llega a la plataforma que también compró los derechos del Mundial 2030
La velada del año se retransmitirá en Netflix durante los próximos tres años (ediciones de 2027, 2028 y 2029), marcando un nuevo capítulo en la historia del evento creado por Ibai Llanos y ampliando su alcance a una audiencia global, ha anunciado este lunes la plataforma de contenidos. Lo ha hecho solo unos días después de confirmar que ha comprado los derechos de emisión del Mundial 2030.
La velada del año es desde hace varias temporadas uno de los mayores eventos de streaming en español. La quinta edición, en 2025, alcanzó un pico de 9,3 millones de espectadores simultáneos, y la audiencia media ha pasado de cerca de 1 millón en 2021 a más de 6 millones en 2026, apunta Netflix en su nota.
El propio Llanos lo ha confirmado a través de un vídeo en sus redes sociales.
La Velada del Año x Netflix. Historia.
2027
2028
2029 pic.twitter.com/bQa6D5QsOz
— Ibai (@IbaiLlanos) October 19, 2026
Lo que comenzó como un evento de boxeo entre creadores de contenido de España y América Latina se ha convertido en un espectáculo más ambicioso, que incorpora actuaciones musicales y reúne a otros invitados de la industria del entretenimiento y la música. En sus últimas ediciones, se ha organizado en grandes recintos, como el estadio Metropolitano de Madrid, el Santiago Bernabéu y La Cartuja de Sevilla.
Hasta ahora, La velada del año se había retransmitido principalmente en Twitch, a través del canal de Ibai Llanos. En 2026, la sexta edición amplió su distribución a YouTube y TikTok, antes de iniciar una nueva etapa en Netflix a partir de 2027.
De esta forma, Netflix sigue ampliando su apuesta por emitir en directo eventos de masas. Ofrecerá en directo los 104 partidos de la competición. Otra cadena nacional dará en abierto un paquete de encuentros, entre ellos, los de España, como ha ocurrido este verano con DAZN y TVE.

title: Boland exposes South Africa's frailties to give Robinson blueprint
summary: Boland exposes South Africa's frailties to give Robinson blueprint - Published Second Test, Gqeberha (day two of five) South Africa 97-5: Bavuma 41*; Boland 4-31 Australia: Yet to bat For much of Monday it appeared rain would deny any meaningful play taking place on day two of the second Test betwee...
content:
Boland exposes South Africa's frailties to give Robinson blueprint
- Published
Second Test, Gqeberha (day two of five)
South Africa 97-5: Bavuma 41*; Boland 4-31
Australia: Yet to bat
For much of Monday it appeared rain would deny any meaningful play taking place on day two of the second Test between South Africa and Australia.
In the end, the hosts may have wished that remained the case as their top-order frailties were exposed once again in Gqeberha.
With the Proteas 97-5 at the close, the balance of power in the series remains firmly with Australia.
It took Australia's metronome Scott Boland only seven deliveries to add to his two wickets taken amid the rain on day one.
Relentless in his line and lengths, the 37-year-old found the perfect length to drag debutant Marques Ackerman onto the front foot.
Ackerman defended nicely for 38 balls but here he neither defended nor unleashed a drive.
Instead, he stumbled forward and became the 85th victim of Boland's 20-Test career as he nicked through to wicketkeeper Alex Carey.
Boland ended the day with 4-31 as he, once again, emphatically pushed his case.
That Ackerman, one of two batting changes from their first-Test defeat, was opening the batting against the red ball for the first time in his career pointed to the issues South Africa face.
The other new face, Matthew Breetzke, was brought in on the back of his white-ball form after Tristan Stubbs played two poor strokes in the first Test.
Breetzke's feet barely moved in making four from 17. He was eventually dismissed trying to force Mitchell Starc loosely through the covers off the back foot.
A result of Ackerman's selection was Ryan Rickelton, another fine white-ball player with a modest red-ball record, being moved from opener to number six and wicketkeeper.
After top-edging a pull last week, he was worked over by Pat Cummins' bouncers late on day two.
He had already been hit on the body and dropped on 26 by Marnus Labuschagne when, stuck on the crease, he edged Boland while pushing tentatively outside off stump.
On another day the ball would have found the turf but Matt Renshaw stuck out a right hand at first slip and somehow scooped the ball up above the ground.
Boland's familiar attack
1 of 4
Boland's Test bowling average now stands at 18.08. No bowler since the First World War has taken as many wickets at a better rate.
His probing has ensured Australia have not missed spinner Nathan Lyon, who he replaced, or Josh Hazlewood, who remained at the team hotel throughout the day because of illness.
Of Boland's 84 deliveries across this innings, 63% of his deliveries were on a good line and length, while 24% of those would have gone on to hit the stumps.
On the latter metric, Cummins has the next best record but lags behind at 12%.
Whether Boland has proven yet again he is ideal for seaming conditions or that he is deserving of more more opportunities can be debated. Ollie Robinson, who bowls a similar style, will surely have taken note as he prepares for England's tour of South Africa back home.
With the weather set to improve, the Proteas have three days remaining in this Test to reverse the momentum of the series which only appears to be heading in one direction.
Much will depend on Temba Bavuma, who remained on 41 not out, and seamer Kagiso Rabada.
Rabada returned match figures of 11-150 against Australia on this ground in 2018 - a South Africa win which levelled that four-match series going into the infamous Sandpaper Test.
The hosts may need similar and more here because right now their batting does not appear up to the test.

title: Amazon to fund 12 small nuclear reactors at former Indiana coal plant
summary: Amazon is funding development of a proposed 960-megawatt nuclear plant in Indiana and would be the first customer to buy its power, the companies announced Monday. Utility company American Electric Power (AEP) would operate the plant. X-energy, which designs small modular nuclear reactors and went p...
content:
Amazon is funding development of a proposed 960-megawatt nuclear plant in Indiana and would be the first customer to buy its power, the companies announced Monday. Utility company American Electric Power (AEP) would operate the plant. X-energy, which designs small modular nuclear reactors and went public in April, would supply the reactors.
The new power plant would consist of 12 Xe-100 small modular reactors and be located on the site of a demolished coal power plant just south of Terre Haute. The deal is the second commercial agreement between Amazon and X-energy, and it’s three times larger than the first, which was announced two years ago.
Amazon has invested heavily in X-energy, leading a $700 million Series C-1 round in October 2024. The two companies have said they ultimately plan to build 5 gigawatts of new nuclear generating capacity in the U.S. by 2039.
Unlike many newly announced power plants, these reactors would be connected to the public electric grid, though Amazon says the power would also serve its data centers.
The companies’ aggressive timeline still depends on X-energy successfully delivering its first power plant at a Dow Chemical plant southeast of Houston, Texas. The site, called Seadrift, has recently been at the center of a lawsuit filed by the state of Texas, which accuses the plant of “habitual non-compliance” with water and solid-waste regulations and permits.
X-energy has yet to break ground at Seadrift, which will host four Xe-100 reactors to provide the chemical plant with heat and electricity. The company said its construction permit is in the final phases of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s review process.
Startups and large cloud computing companies are betting that small modular reactors (SMRs), like the kind being developed by X-energy, will help pull the nuclear industry out of its slump. The most recent nuclear power plants built in the U.S. suffered from egregious budget overruns and slipped timelines.
By shrinking the reactor, companies like X-energy hope that mass manufacturing will keep costs and schedules in line. Even then, it could be a tall order. Experts say mass manufacturing often doesn’t start producing benefits for about a decade.
X-energy debuted on the Nasdaq in April in an IPO priced at $23 per share. Investor excitement drove the price up 27% in the first day of trading, but shares of the newly public company have dropped by nearly two-thirds since then.
News of the Amazon deal sent X-energy’s shares up about 10% in premarket trading, though they were down by less than 2% at the time of publication.

title: Guehi among players not to take knee - is it time to 'move campaign along'?
summary: Guehi among players not to take knee - is it time to 'move campaign along'? - Published Premier League clubs took the knee this weekend for the first time this season as part of October's No Room for Racism campaign. But six players across five clubs chose to remain standing during the pre-match ges...
content:
Guehi among players not to take knee - is it time to 'move campaign along'?
- Published
Premier League clubs took the knee this weekend for the first time this season as part of October's No Room for Racism campaign.
But six players across five clubs chose to remain standing during the pre-match gesture:
- Tyler Adams (Bournemouth)
- Rayan (Bournemouth)
- Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds)
- Issa Diop (Ipswich)
- Marc Guehi (Manchester City)
- Ainsley Maitland-Niles (Everton)
Speaking before Manchester City's Champions League game on Tuesday, Guehi was asked whether it had lost its impact.
"I haven't been taking the knee for a while now. I always clap, just because of what that actually signifies," said the England international.
"I don't think it's necessarily a football issue, I think it's a wider societal issue and football is just that beacon of hope to try and get the message out.
"The message is still there, which is great. More can always be done. I think we should see how we can move the campaign along."
The Premier League maintains that taking the knee is a decision led by the players and that it is supportive of whatever stance they choose to take.
- Why are Premier League clubs still taking the knee? 
  - Published17 October 2025
How did the campaign begin?
Premier League players began taking the knee in 2020 following the death of George Floyd and the subsequent Black Lives Matter protests.
The campaign was limited to selected matches following an agreement by club captains before the 2022-23 campaign.
This season, captains agreed to take the knee during October's No Room For Racism fixtures, which coincide with Black History Month in the UK.
The other five players who did not take the knee this weekend have not publicly commented, but Leeds manager Daniel Farke explained Calvert-Lewin's position.
"Dom is more or less like, 'no, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up'. Every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way," said Farke.
"It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together."
Former Crystal Palace forward Wilfried Zaha became the first Premier League player to stop taking the knee in 2021.
"I feel kneeling has just become a part of the pre-match routine and at the moment it doesn't matter whether we kneel or stand, some of us still continue to receive abuse," he said at the time.
Has it made a difference?
Announcing this month's campaign,, external the Premier League said: "Players will be taking the knee before kick-off during the next two match rounds to show unity against all forms of discrimination."
Kick It Out told BBC Sport that taking the knee "still has value in raising awareness of the structural inequalities that exist in football and society."
"We can also understand the reasons players might become frustrated with the pace of change," they added.
Between 2021-22 and 2025-26, reports of both discrimination and racism received by the charity more than doubled, and reached record levels last season.
High-profile cases have also highlighted the continuing abuse faced by players.
After England defender Jess Carter received racist abuse online during last summer's Women's Euros, the Lionesses stopped taking the knee.
"Taking the knee, that's not enough. We have done that for a while. The impact is not good enough, it's not as big as we think," said England manager Sarina Wiegman at the time.
In February, Burnley midfielder Hannibal Mejbri, Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana, Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare and Sunderland winger Romaine Mundle were all subjected to racist abuse on social media over a single weekend.
A BBC Sport investigation also identified 22,389 potentially abusive messages across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and X over a separate weekend.
Nevertheless, 2025 YouGov polling, external found a majority of ethnic minority football fans in Britain still considered taking the knee important in tackling racism - although most football fans overall in England did not.
The No Room For Racism campaign extends beyond taking the knee.
"We are using the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism," said Premier League chief executive Richard Masters.
Players have also helped develop educational resources about diversity, available to more than 19,000 primary schools across England and Wales.
"I think it's important for young people to see role models who look like them, to see that they can achieve anything. It doesn't matter who you are, what you do or how you look," said Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk as part of the campaign.
"It means a lot to me to represent my community on and off the pitch."

- Published
Brentford say they are working with the police following a "dangerous" incident in which a rugby ball was kicked from a height towards the pitch during their Premier League game with Liverpool.
A video on social media shows a man standing on a rooftop near the Gtech Community Stadium, kicking a rugby ball towards the pitch while others laugh and cheer.
Another clip from inside the ground shows the rugby ball being taken away from the pitch by a member of staff as play continued.
In a statement, Brentford, who were beaten 2-1 on Saturday, said "such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful".
"The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution," the statement added.
"The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken."
Brentford, who had Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt both sent off in the second half, are sixth in the league table after the defeat.

title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
summary: The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more....
content:
The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.
One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.”
Another, “cleanyourtv,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.
While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone. With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits.
Modern smart TVs ship with a technology called automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what’s playing on the screen using screenshots, audio clips, or other forms of digital fingerprinting.
If these “dumb TV” hacks become more popular among everyday consumers, they have the potential to disrupt the smart TV ad industry, which profits from selling viewing data to advertisers or using it to display personalized ads on their own interfaces.
As the creator of cleanyourtv, Gathin T., puts it, the idea to clean up the smart TV interface started one afternoon when he got tired of seeing the ads on his parents’ TV set.
“I had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi and build a simple home screen with just their apps on it. I put the prompt on GitHub, tweeted the before and after, and a few thousand people did the same to their own TVs over the next two days. Xiaomi, TCL, Sony, Fire TV, LG, a projector or two,” the developer wrote on a website for donations, linked from the project’s homepage.
The solution doesn’t require gaining root access to the TV, nor does it make it impossible to return to the factory default state, if desired.
Meanwhile, the dumbtv solution has been tested end-to-end on a Fire TV Edition television set and Android/Google TV platforms on TVs from Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense, Xiaomi, and Shield. To use this hack, the developer, Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, suggests pointing your preferred AI agent at the dumbtv repository on GitHub.
Sabuwala said he was motivated to work on dumbtv because he was tired of the ads and not being able to delve directly into the content he wanted to watch. His solution was coded using a combination of Deepseek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, he told TechCrunch, and he plans to maintain the GitHub, adding support for more models over time.
Fair warning: All these solutions are works in progress, and various users are now testing them across different TV platforms and suggesting updates and fixes.
However, individuals don’t need to borrow someone else’s work from GitHub to get the job done.
In one newly viral X post, Ryan Doyle explains that he simply sent Claude Code the listing for his TV and asked “Can you hack this?” The agent then talked him through the process, allowing him to remove the ads and bloatware from the TV set, speed up the lagging user interface, and customize his screensaver, he claims.
Doyle then goes on to demonstrate in a video how fast and responsive the new interface is after the AI made the requested changes.
Seeing posts about people “vibe-coding their TVs,” inspired one X user, Mihir Gupta, to try it himself.
“One afternoon with Claude Code: 25 bloat apps disabled, the 192 MB stock launcher replaced with a custom 83 MB one, plus rotating wallpapers,” he wrote.
The end result of these hacks may be mixed, however. Some people have found that Claude wouldn’t respond to their simple suggestions to “hack my TV,” necessitating more complex prompts. Others warned that AI agents could make mistakes, possibly disabling important packages or breaking things in the process. One person even said they bricked their Android TV using Claude, and another got stuck halfway through hacking their Fire TV.
For those wary of using AI to fully hack their TVs, there are existing solutions for customizing Android-based smart TVs, such as home screen replacement apps ATV Launcher, Projectivy Launcher, and FLauncher.

title: La policía carga contra un grupo de profesores de Madrid que bloqueaba la entrada a un acto de Ayuso
summary: La policía carga contra un grupo de profesores de Madrid que bloqueaba la entrada a un acto de Ayuso Cancelado un acto de la consejera de Educación de Madrid, Mercedes Zarzalejo, en un centro de FP por la presencia de manifestantes Unos 500 profesores partícipes de la huelga educativa madrileña han ...
content:
La policía carga contra un grupo de profesores de Madrid que bloqueaba la entrada a un acto de Ayuso
Cancelado un acto de la consejera de Educación de Madrid, Mercedes Zarzalejo, en un centro de FP por la presencia de manifestantes
Unos 500 profesores partícipes de la huelga educativa madrileña han acudido este lunes, en torno a las dos de la tarde, a protestar a un acto celebrado en el Palacio de Santoña, en el centro de Madrid, en el que participaba la presidenta de la Comunidad, Isabel Díaz Ayuso. Los manifestantes venían de concentrarse frente a la Consejería de Educación en la calle Alcalá 42, donde han rodeado la puerta de entrada mientras una docena de policías protegía el acceso. “Ayuso da la cara”, “Zarzalejo, vaya tela, tus mentiras ya no cuelan”, gritaban, en referencia a la presidenta y su consejera de Educación, Mercedes Zarzalejo. Para despejar la salida del edificio, varias decenas de antidisturbios han llegado al lugar y, ante la negativa a marcharse de los manifestantes, han comenzado a cargar para desplazarlos varios metros hasta dejarlos concentrados en la intersección con la calle Príncipe. “¡Huelga, huelga, huelga indefinida!” y “Ayuso, escucha, la pública está en lucha”, gritaban. A las 14.13, Ayuso consiguió salir del edificio por el otro extremo de la calle, donde no quedaba ningún manifestante, y se marchó en su coche oficial.
Se dieron momentos de mucha tensión. La calle de las Huertas, donde se encuentra el Palacio de Santoña, es estrecha y sin apenas tráfico de coches. Una especie de ratonera para los cientos de personas que esperaban a la presidenta. La huelga educativa ha vivido una mañana muy agitada en torno a los dos nombres propios más repetidos desde el inicio de la movilización el pasado 14 de octubre: Ayuso y Zarzalejo, las dos personas que concentran la ira de los huelguistas. “No quieren paz en las calles, quieren París”, ha tuiteado la consejera después de los incidentes en referencia a la violencia que se ha vivido estos días en Francia.
Horas antes, era Zarzalejo quien veía cómo otros cientos de manifestantes acudían a un acto suyo en el instituto público de Formación Profesional Antonio Palacios, en Vallecas. Una sonora pitada recibía al vehículo en el que viajaba un representante de la Consejería de Educación de la Comunidad de Madrid a su llegada al centro y, ante el ambiente caldeado, se decidió anular la visita de la consejera, que no llegó ni a acercarse al lugar. La Policía Nacional contuvo sin incidentes a los huelguistas, que gritaban al unísono: “¿Dónde está Zarzalejo, Zarzalejo dónde está?”, “Siéntate, Zarzalejo, Zarzalejo, siéntate”, “Somos docentes, no delincuentes”, “Educación pública”, “Esto también es por vuestros hijos”, “Huelga indefinida” o “La lucha es el único camino”.
La Comunidad de Madrid ha asegurado en un comunicado que lamenta “profundamente la radicalización de estas protestas, que en apenas cuatro días han perdido la mayor parte del apoyo de los docentes en las aulas, pasando del 44,6% de seguimiento del pasado miércoles al 13,2% de hoy [lunes], pero que algunos siguen empeñados en trasladar a las calles para impedir el desarrollo normal de la actividad en los centros y seguir tomando como rehenes a los alumnos, a sus familias, a los docentes y a toda la ciudadanía”. Las centrales sindicales que han convocado los paros cifran el seguimiento de la huelga este lunes en más de un 50%, tras calcular un 72% en la primera jornada.
A primera hora de la mañana, en otro punto de la capital —en el distrito de Moratalaz—, otro grupo de huelguistas ha cortado la autovía A-3 en sentido Madrid. El tráfico ha permanecido detenido durante 30 minutos por la presencia de los manifestantes y de decenas de pupitres y sillas de colegio que han colocado en medio de la carretera. “La educación pública no se vende, la educación pública se defiende” o “el ático de Ayuso para 3º B”, gritaban. La protesta ha sido encabezada por dos pancartas principales, una bajo el lema “Educación pública en huelga” y otra “Su bienestar no puede esperar, su bienestar también importa”.
¿Qué piden los huelguistas?
Las seis exigencias principales que empujan esta huelga son: reducir a 17 las horas de clase a la semana en secundaria y a 22 en infantil y primaria (desde 19 y 25 horas, respectivamente); bajar las ratios de estudiantes por clase, incrementando el personal especializado en atención a la diversidad; atajar la segregación socioeconómica del alumnado entre la red pública y concertada; aumentar el salario de los docentes en 600 euros al mes; disminuir la carga burocrática y mejorar las infraestructuras educativas, incluyendo la climatización de los centros y la eliminación de amianto.
La huelga indefinida por la educación pública ha entrado en una nueva fase desde este lunes. Las tres primeras jornadas fueron un “éxito” según los sindicatos convocantes, que cifraron su seguimiento en un 72% el miércoles, y un 60% el jueves y el viernes, además de dos grandes manifestaciones desde Atocha hasta Sol el miércoles y el viernes que congregaron 25.000 y 35.000 personas respectivamente, según datos de la Delegación de Gobierno. A partir de ahora, los 65.000 profesores de enseñanzas no universitarias llamados a la huelga, que dan clase a más de 660.000 alumnos en toda la Comunidad de Madrid, deben decidir si mantener el pulso con la misma intensidad que hasta ahora. Los sindicatos convocantes —CC OO, UGT, STEM, CGT, CNT y Solidaridad Obrera, además de otros colectivos y plataformas docentes como CSIF, que ha convocado huelga al margen de la movilización unitaria― consideran que el momento para la movilización es “ahora”.
Concentración ante la consejería
Antes de las cargas policiales en el acto de Ayuso, hacia el mediodía, unas 2.000 personas se han concentrado frente a la sede de la Consejería de Educación, en la calle de Alcalá. Centenares de profesores vestidos con camisetas de color verde han llegado desde la Puerta del Sol, el metro Sevilla y la glorieta de C

title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
summary: Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise. While it uses fewer parameters than the Nemotron 3 Ultra model, Nvidia says it can deliver ...
content:
Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing.
The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a large, 120-billion-parameter model geared for agents used by the enterprise. While it uses fewer parameters than the Nemotron 3 Ultra model, Nvidia says it can deliver similar accuracy in instruction-following and tool-use tasks.
At the other end of the spectrum, the company also launched two lightweight Bolt models. These are intended to run locally on the new AI PCs (running the Nvidia RTX Spark chip) and workstations running the DGX Spark. Such PCs, aimed at consumers, programmers, and enterprise knowledge workers, are being released right now into the market through partners like Microsoft and Dell.
“Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models.
Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks. These tasks include document intelligence, financial accounting, scientific experimentation, medical insurance claims, and security attack resilience.
While such claims are standard whenever a major tech company announces a new model, Nvidia has backed it up with a list of heavy-hitter companies that it says are using Super VL. These include Skydance, EY, Ramp, Crowdstrike, Perplexity, and Salesforce.
Of course, these aren’t the first open-weight models that Nvidia has released that compete with the proprietary frontier labs — companies that are both its customers and its investments. The GPU giant has an entire family of Nemotron models that do everything from multimodal artificial intelligence to reasoning, coding, math, and enterprise automation.
However, those fast-growing proprietary AI labs are now looking to many other chips and AI system makers beyond Nvidia to power their needs, like AWS’s Trainium and Cerebras, as well as building their own home-grown chips.
So Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers. “Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and own what they build,” Briski wrote.
But with the announcement or the smaller, local PC models, it is also trying to push forward the nascent trend of consumer AI assistants. While it seems a new AI assistant is introduced every day by startups and Big Tech alike, privacy-weary consumers may not want to invite such agents so deeply into their lives giving them access to info about their families, health, finances, and so on.
So, while Nvidia hopes to create a new market for itself selling PCs powered by its chips by creating machines that run the models and agents locally, PC users “can delegate everyday projects … without sending those workloads to the cloud,” Briski wrote.
Of the two Bolt models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74-billion parameter model designed for local agentic tasks. It is intended to balance speed with reasoning to handle multistep reasoning, tool calling, and web browsing. The smallest Bolt E4B is aimed at conversational agents.
Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming later this month, Nvidia says.
